oracle.description: Hand-crafted 264-byte MLV file (poc.mlv): 52-byte MLVI header declaring video class LJ92|RAW (codec_id TIFF), 180-byte RAWI block (width=height=16, bits_per_coded_sample=16), and a 32-byte VIDF block whose declared block size (120) and 'space' field (2140) make the unsigned subtraction `size -= space` in read_packet() underflow to 4294965256. That value is passed unchanged into get_packet_lj92(..., int64_t size); `av_new_packet(pkt, size + MAX_HEADER_SIZE)` truncates the 64-bit sum to a 32-bit int, wrapping to 8, so only a tiny (8-byte, 72-byte incl. redzone/padding) packet buffer is allocated while bytestream2_init_writer() is told it has the full 2048-byte MAX_HEADER_SIZE to write TIFF/DNG header fields into — causing a heap-buffer-overflow write. Reproduced with: /work/ffmpeg -y -f mlv -i /poc/poc.mlv -c copy -f null -
